To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a control strategy for SMSEs that is robust to sources and load fluctuations.
we propose an adaptive generalized PID controllers and a fuzzy logic coordinator to control the energy transfers in an LTV SMSE.
the adaptive generalized PID controllers provide an effective regulation of the SMSE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of a LTV system with a fuzzy logic controller.
the design of a control strategy that ensures the stability and robustness of SMSE and the satisfaction of the load requirements whatever the sources and the load fluctuations.
the control of a SMSE composed by a DC bus, a set of sources (solar, wind, fuel cell, etc.) and a set of loads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed control strategy is a promising approach for the control of the DC bus voltage, the currents provided by the sources and the power ratio in the considered SMSE.
the proposed control scheme is a good candidate for SMSE control.
the proposed control strategy is very effective and robust for the load sharing in SMSES.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new adaptive generalized PID control for the DC bus voltage regulation and a fuzzy logic coordinator for the power distribution in the considered SMSE.
a fuzzy logic coordinator is proposed to control the energy transfers in a SMSE.
a fuzzy logic coordinator is proposed to control the load sharing among the different sources of a SMSE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed controller can be easily adapted to any kind of sources, loads and control requirements.
the proposed adaptive generalized PID control scheme can handle the LTV system and the fuzzy logic coordinator can tune the power ratio provided to the load according to the load variations.
the proposed control strategy is simple, robust to load and sources fluctuations, and can be implemented with low-cost microcontrollers.
